key_insight: Adding GPT-4o–extracted deficits from physical therapy notes increased frailty identification but did not significantly improve prognostic discrimination.
clinical_relevance: LLM-enhanced frailty assessment identified more hospitalizations associated with adverse outcomes, with higher sensitivity but lower specificity than the standard index.
method: Retrospective cohort of 616 hospitalizations among adults aged ≥50 years at two affiliated hospitals.
Compared a validated 35-deficit electronic frailty index with an enhanced version incorporating GPT-4o–extracted deficits.
Evaluated associations and AUROC for discharge to a facility, readmission, or death within 90 days.
evidence_signal: Frailty classification increased from 35.1% to 58.8% and sensitivity from 42.5% to 69.4%, while specificity fell from 73.0% to 52.7%; AUROC increased from 0.636 to 0.660 without statistical significance (p=0.12).
watch_item: Physical therapy documentation was available for only 53.4% of hospitalizations, potentially limiting the consistency of LLM enhancement.
paper_title: Large Language Model-Enhanced Electronic Frailty Assessment and Prognostic Performance in Hospitalized Adults: A Retrospective Cohort Study
